title: Distinct components of a Noetherian curve meet in finitely many closed points
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] with topological Krull dimension $\dim Y\le 1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Its irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] form a finite family. For two distinct components $Z_i,Z_j$, every point of $Z_i\cap Z_j$ is closed in $Y$ and the intersection is finite. Consequently the union $T=\bigcup_{i\ne j}(Z_i\cap Z_j)$ is a finite set of closed points; if $y\notin T$, it lies on exactly one component.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX (varieties-lemma-dim-1-noetherian-reduced-separated-has-ample), proof, first paragraph, finiteness and closedness of T

proof.text: The irreducible components of Y form a finite family by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components].

source.place: Properties Lemma 0BA8, finiteness of irreducible components

proof.text: Fix distinct components $Z_i\neq Z_j$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] $Z_i$ has a generic point $\eta_i$ with $Z_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}$, and generic points are unique; hence two distinct points of $Y$ have distinct closures, so $Y$ is Kolmogorov, and so is its subspace $Z_i$ (an open of $Z_i$ is the trace of an open of $Y$). The point $\eta_i$ is not in $Z_j$, since otherwise $Z_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}\subseteq Z_j$, and maximality of the irreducible subset $Z_i$ would give $Z_i=Z_j$. Thus $U=Z_i\setminus Z_j$ is a nonempty open subset of $Z_i$, which is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components], and $\dim Z_i\le\dim Y\le1$ because a chain of irreducible closed subsets of the closed subspace $Z_i$ is such a chain in $Y$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Every point $x$ of $Z_i\cap Z_j$ lies outside $U$, so [lem-sc-dim-one-point-outside-open-closed], applied to $Z_i$, says that $\{x\}$ is closed in $Z_i$; because $Z_i$ is closed in $Y$, $\{x\}$ is closed in $Y$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX proof, first paragraph: distinct components have proper intersections and points in them are closed; the generic-point argument is written out here

proof.text: The intersection $Z_i\cap Z_j$ is a closed subset of $Y$ and all its points are closed in $Y$ by step 2. Therefore [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite] makes $Z_i\cap Z_j$ finite. Taking the finite union over the finite family of ordered pairs $i\neq j$ (step 1) gives a finite set $T$ of closed points. Every point $y\in Y$ lies on some irreducible component by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]; if $y\notin T$ lay on two distinct components, it would belong to their intersection and hence to $T$; therefore $y$ lies on exactly one component.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX proof, first paragraph: T is finite and consists of closed points, and points outside T lie on a unique component
